target_customer: SaaS companies that want an AI agent inside their own product
problem: Calling a model is easy, but shipping an in-product agent needs streaming, crash recovery, guardrails, matching UI and current product knowledge. Teaflask provides that layer without backend changes.
business_model: Developer platform with free start and enterprise sales; model usage on developer key, credits or user plan
product_category: In-product AI agent infrastructure for SaaS

founders.name: Ragav Sachdeva
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page; sole founder.

competitors.name: CopilotKit
competitors.what: Open-source framework for embedded copilots in React apps
competitors.traction_then: tens of thousands of GitHub stars (counts vary by source)

competitors.name: Yedric
competitors.what: Embeddable agent turning natural language into in-app actions

competitors.name: Paragon
competitors.what: Embedded integration platform for SaaS developers

technical_complexity.rationale: Durable agent execution, action scanning from product code, permission controls and sandboxing are real engineering, but built on existing model APIs by one founder.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integration into a customer's product could create switching costs, but open-source alternatives exist and frontier labs could ship similar tooling.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early; adjacent players already sell embedded agent frameworks.

market_need_then: SaaS companies are under pressure to add agents; a 2026 guide defines in-app agents as a category and comparison sites note teams still need backend tools, permissions and safety design.

identity.logo: Light and dark logo variants; no further description
identity.visual_style: Product screenshots and card-style feature blocks

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable but unrelated tea and flask name; a single Fondo article was the only press found and no community evidence.

outcome_analysis: Teaflask joined YC in Spring 2026 as a one-person company with a technical founder and a product that is live per its site. No outcome yet; its fate depends on winning SaaS customers against open-source frameworks and on whether model providers absorb the in-app agent layer.
notes: Dealroom lists a $125k seed with no investors or date; unverified aggregator figure, not recorded as a round. Competitors are from 2026 comparison pages that lack exact dates.
